candidates.title: Alignment
candidates.summary: The Alignment team works to understand the risks of AI models and develops ways to ensure that future ones remain helpful, honest, and harmless. We also work to develop and implement the ideal persona for our AI assistant, Claude. Team blog Visit Alignment training Our researchers develop methods, environments, and datasets for training Claude to be helpful, harmless, and honest. We also research and attempt to implement the ideal “assistant” persona for our models. Evaluation and oversight We test to ensure our models remain honest and harmless under a broad range of circumstances, and work to understand and manage the risks of unexpected model behavior, through work on the models themselves and the safety structures we build around them. candidates.title: MetaFORGE: A Meta-Learning Framework for Harness Optimization in Automated Code Generation for Parallel Computing
candidates.summary: Large language models (LLMs) can generate parallel programs, but their correctness and performance depend strongly on the instructions that guide generation. We present \textsc{MetaFORGE}, an execution-grounded meta-learning framework that iteratively optimizes persistent natural-language skill specifications for MPI C code generation. \textsc{MetaFORGE} combines correctness testing, compiler diagnostics, static-analysis findings, runtime measurements, and rank-level load-imbalance profiles into a scalar reward that drives textual-gradient refinement, while an external memory distills and retrieves reward-supported optimization knowledge across runs. Across six MPI tasks and three workload sizes, \textsc{MetaFORGE} improves static-analysis quality, runtime, and load balance relative to zero-shot generation and generally exceeds the evaluated \textsc{TextGrad} iterative baseline. A model-matched refinement ablation shows that the MetaFORGE advantage persists when its refinement model is reduced to \texttt{gpt-4o}. An expanded retrieval ablation across all 18 task--workload configurations shows consistent runtime benefit and broad static-analysis and load-balance benefit from retrieved context. Leakage-controlled held-out and zero-update experiments further provide evidence that optimization knowledge persists in both the transferred skill and external memory under the evaluated protocol.

candidates.title: GREMLIN: Generating Random Environments for Meta-Learning with Interacting Networks
candidates.summary: Can randomly parameterized neural environments supply useful experience for learning a reinforcement learning algorithm? We investigate this question using DiscoRL's rule-discovery framework, replacing human-designed training games with sixteen selected neural environments. Each game combines bounded vector dynamics with a random strategy-based reward and an independent outcome reward. After 224.8 million agent-environment steps, we froze the teacher and trained fresh agents. DQN outscored GREMLIN on most games, both generated and human-designed. GREMLIN nevertheless outperformed the untrained teacher on all 26 games, showing that generated experience can improve a learning rule. It remains unclear whether this approach can yield a competitive rule with longer meta-training.

candidates.title: 当你的下一位客户是 AI Agent：企业营销与销售的 AI 发展前景
candidates.summary:
购买行为正在进入一个全新时代。AI Agent 开始影响消费者发现、评估、比较和选择产品的方式。在消费者访问网站或与销售人员交流之前，Agent 就已经阅读品牌发布的内容、汇总不同选项，并帮助消费者缩小选择范围。

与此同时，营销和销售组织也在利用 AI 推动自身转型，将过去由一系列营销活动和销售策略组成的工作模式，升级为能够持续运行的增长体系。这一体系能够深入理解客户需求、优先识别高价值商机，并实时加速营收增长。

这两场变革正在同步发生，并深刻改变着企业创造市场需求和赢得客户的方式。

当品牌信息的第一位“读者”变成机器，品牌建设、内容营销和需求开发将发生怎样的变化？企业如何确保自身能够被 AI 发现，并在 AI 生成的推荐结果中赢得信任？当买卖双方都开始使用 AI Agent，客户关系又将如何演变？

哪些营销和销售工作流应该率先重新设计？相关岗位与技能又该如何随之调整？企业领导者应如何判断，AI 究竟带来了真正的业务成效，还是仅仅让业务活动变得更加频繁？
